portada.titular: Canada expands AI computing fund to $1 billion
portada.resumen: On November 26, Ottawa announced a $700 million expansion of its AI Compute Access Fund. Eligible small and medium-sized businesses can receive support covering up to 80% of eligible computing costs when using a sovereign Canadian provider, compared with up to 50% for other eligible cloud services.
portada.para_ti: Lower computing costs could help Canadian firms develop AI products without relying entirely on foreign infrastructure.

items.titular: Federal funding reaches 45 more Canadian companies
items.resumen: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada announced more than $52 million for 45 recipients on November 26 under the AI Compute Access Fund.
items.para_ti: The awards help smaller firms access computing resources; they do not guarantee commercial success or new jobs.

items.titular: AI chip demand lifts Taiwan's growth forecast
items.resumen: Reuters reported on November 27 that Taiwan's government raised its 2026 economic growth forecast from 11.05% to 13.28%, citing strong AI demand. Trade restrictions remain a risk.
items.para_ti: Demand for AI hardware is affecting entire economies, although forecasts are not final results.

items.titular: XPENG outlines next steps for physical AI
items.resumen: At the Guangzhou Auto Show on November 27, XPENG outlined its 2027 expansion plans for AI-powered vehicles, humanoid robots and autonomous mobility.
items.para_ti: The announcement shows how vehicle and robotics development are converging. A company roadmap is not proof of reliable deployment.

items.titular: SAP reportedly weighs major workforce reductions
items.resumen: Reuters reported on November 27 that SAP is considering substantial job reductions as AI changes the software industry. The restructuring is under consideration, not a confirmed final decision.
items.para_ti: Even skilled software workers may face changing responsibilities as employers adopt AI. Proposed cuts should not be counted as actual job losses.

palabra.definicion: Computing infrastructure under domestic ownership or control, intended to give a country greater control over access, operations and data governance.
